correctness.rationale: Coarea gives exactly \(V_n(s)=s f_n(s)/n\), and strict concavity of \(\log s+\log f_n(s)\) proves a unique off-center maximum for every \(n\ge3\). A differentiated uniform Fourier expansion through \(n^{-2}\) gives the stationarity shift \(1/6+2/(45n)+O(n^{-2})\), the relative volume \(1+1/(6n)+7/(120n^2)+O(n^{-3})\), and the absolute volume \(\sqrt{3/(2\pi n)}(1+1/(60n)+73/(3360n^2)+O(n^{-3}))\). Gaussian-moment constants and logarithmic cross-terms were recomputed; 672 finite checks passed. Remainders are proven analytically; numerical samples are not infinite certificates.

value.rationale: The global maximal-volume cube-pyramid problem remains unsolved in general dimension. Its natural body-diagonal subfamily supplies explicit sharp lower bounds. Unlike the known qualitative improvement over the central-section pyramid, this theorem completely determines its unique off-center maximizing section and quantifies displacement and relative volume enhancement through two asymptotic orders. The results are structurally motivated, not a routine single-number recomputation.
